answer: Sybil resistance comes from a mandatory per-identity stake: before an agent can attest or earn, it must lock a bond into a vault. To flood the network with fakes, an attacker needs one separate bond for every forged identity, so cost grows linearly with army size, while an honest agent pays only once. Caught fraud slashes that bond, making each fake a net loss. Even a shifting dune of thousands of bogus nodes cannot repay its stakes, and the crystal rule that identity requires real capital keeps the economy defensible.
